amrex::DistributionMapping dm_full_domain
 the DistributionMapping every full-domain multifab is built on. Each of those covers the domain in a single box, so the map holds one entry, and which rank it names is whichever holds the least fab memory when it is built. Building one per allocator therefore put the mask and the data it weights on different ranks under MPI. Empty until full_domain_dmap first needs it.

bool time_interp_flux = false
 interpolate the parent's barotropic mass flux in time at the coarse-fine interface, rather than holding its step average. Off matches most ROMS configurations.
 
int cf_impose_flux = 0
 impose the parent's barotropic mass flux on DUon/DVom at the coarse-fine interface, rather than relying on the velocity written by set_2d_cf_bcs being turned back into the same flux. Off by default: it improves conservation but does not cure the two-level barotropic instability seen in Channel_Test.
 
int do_reflux = 1
 correct the coarse tracer with the finer level's accumulated advective flux at their interface. Only has an effect under remora.do_substep with two-way coupling.
 
int cf_avgdown_perimeter = 1
 exclude the coarse-fine perimeter's normal-velocity faces from the fine-to-coarse average, as ROMS does. 1 (default) matches ROMS; 0 includes the perimeter faces in the average.
 
int cf_fill_vel_after = 0
 re-fill the child's 3D velocity from the parent after the step, so the coarse-fine boundary carries the parent's shear profile rather than the one vert_mean_3d left there. Diagnostic; off, so it changes no answer unless set. Both drivers do it only under this knob – see the comment in Advance. On the ratio-3 Dogbone it moves level-1 x-velocity by 4.1e-3 relative and level 0 by 1.9e-4 after 20 steps.
 
int cf_set_2d_bcs = 1
 0 = never impose the 2D coarse-fine interface condition, 1 = every fast step, 2 = only the first fast step of each baroclinic step.
 
int cf_avgdown_bar = 1
 
int cf_fill_all_kcomp = 1
 write every leapfrog record of the coarse-fine ghost band, as put_refine2d does when it sets zeta(:,:,1:3) and Zt_avg1 to one value; without it those records go a whole parent step stale. On by default. Roundoff on the ROMS-matched deck, where the fine zeta halo is barely read, but the dominant cost to volume conservation on the subcycled dogbone: 2.0e-09 to 2.9e-08 of drift over 20 steps, volume being the integral of the free surface this writes. ROMS makes the same trade.
 
int cf_time_interp_zeta = 1
 interpolate the parent in time onto the child's own sub-time, as put_refine2d does, rather than freezing it at the end of the parent step. On by default, and non-conservative for the same reason as cf_fill_all_kcomp: 1.4e-08 of volume drift on its own.
 
int cf_2d_fill_cache = 1
 reuse the coarse-fine ghost values of a fine level's barotropic fills (ubar, vbar, zeta in advance_2d). 0: recompute on every fast step, where the two-level fill re-exchanges and re-interpolates the coarse level each time. 1 (default): compute once per (component, fill time) within a parent step and replay the result; bitwise identical, since the fill reads only the registered coarse data and, for faces, the interface faces FillSet rewrites before every fill, none of which changes inside the parent step. 2: as 1, but also recompute and abort on any difference in the replayed cells. Subcycled driver only.

 per level: the caches for ubar, vbar and zeta (slots 0, 1, 2)
 
amrex::Vector< long > cf_crse_gen
 per level: bumped whenever register_coarse_data hands the level's new state to the next finer level, which invalidates that level's cf_2d_cache
 
int cf_flux_pc = 1
 distribute the parent's interface mass flux piecewise-constantly over the fine faces under each parent face, as ROMS's get_persisted2d does, instead of with the linear tangential variation of AMReX's face interpolator. Both conserve the total; they differ in the profile along the interface. On by default: it removes the fine level's own excess divergence there.
 
int cf_avgdown_stencil = 1
 average the fine velocity onto the coarse over ROMS's nine-point stencil (fine2coarse2d, half-width (Rscale-1)/2 in both directions) instead of only the faces that tile the coarse face. On by default: with cf_flux_pc it takes the interface refinement perturbation from 1.29x ROMS's to 1.01x on the matched dogbone, the residual 1% closing only with cf_impose_flux, which stays off. Not conservative in principle – the nine-point mean does not preserve transport across the interface – but only about 3e-10 of volume drift in practice, well under the free-surface ghost band's cost.
 
int cf_avgdown_volume_weighted = 0
 average the fine tracers onto the coarse weighted by cell volume, Hz/(pm*pn), rather than by area as ROMS's fine2coarse3d does. Off by default. Where the fine layer thickness varies under a coarse cell, as interpolated bathymetry near land makes it, the area mean gains or loses tracer content. Volume weighting keeps it only where the coarse cell's volume matches the fine volumes under it, so not at a coast, and it is not applied to the initial high-resolution cascade (average_down_with_grow_cells).
 
int cf_print_iface = -1
 print the imposed coarse-fine interface velocity at this baroclinic step (-1 = off). Diagnostic only; the fine level is not in the NetCDF output.
 
int reflux_clamp = 1
 stop that correction driving a tracer negative, as ROMS does. On by default to match ROMS; costs exact conservation on any step that clamps.
 
int check_cf_metrics_flag = 0
 measure whether fine cell edges tile the coarse ones at a coarse-fine interface, which is what makes the imposed mass flux conservative

void REMORA::average_down_with_grow_cells ( int  lev,
amrex::Vector< std::unique_ptr< amrex::MultiFab > > &  mf,
bool  use_mask = false 
)

Average down from level lev+1 to lev in mf, including grow cells.

Average a full-domain field from crse_lev+1 onto crse_lev, grow cells included.

With use_mask this takes REMORAMaskedAvgDown's mask-weighted mean instead of the plain one, so the initial state on a coarse cell only partly covered by water comes from that water. It is the formula AverageDownTo applies every step, so the initial and the running state agree on what a land point holds – unless cf_avgdown_volume_weighted is set, which this cascade ignores for want of a full-domain Hz. A two-way run then averages down once before its first step, so only the coarse cells outside the fine grids keep the area mean. Leave use_mask off for grid metrics: a cell size is well defined under land, and masking pm/pn would corrupt it.

Parameters
[in]crse_levlevel to average data down to
[in,out]vec_mfvector over levels of multifabs containing data to average
[in]use_maskweight by the land/sea mask rather than averaging every fine cell

Coarse data ready for a coarse-to-fine interpolation: ghost cells exchanged, and those beyond a wall made to agree with their periodic images.

Coarse data ready for a coarse-to-fine interpolation (FillPatchTwoLevels, InterpFromCoarseLevel), which copies the coarse cells, ghost cells included, with periodicity. The ghost cells are exchanged across grids and periodic edges, and those that also lie beyond a non-periodic domain face are made to agree with their periodic images (periodic_consistent_ghosts), so that no cell of the copy has two different sources (#768, #774, #776). Every coarse-to-fine fill goes through here.

The ghost cells beyond a wall are otherwise taken as the coarse level's own fill left them; they are not refilled from the boundary conditions here.

omega and w for the NetCDF writer, on the s_w points ROMS writes them at.

Both are diagnosed from the current velocities, as ROMS does just before it writes a history record: omega by compute_diagnostic_omega and w by compute_wvel (the same w that z_velocity holds after a step). ◆ estTimeStep()

Real REMORA::estTimeStep ( int  level) const

compute dt from CFL considerations

Estimate the largest stable slow (baroclinic) timestep on a level.

The estimate is the smaller of an advective limit and an external gravity wave limit, each a maximum over the wet cells of the level: 

dt_adv  = cfl / max( |u|*pm, |v|*pn, |w|/Hz )
dt_grav = cfl * ndtfast / max( sqrt(g*|h|) * sqrt(pm^2 + pn^2) )

The second is the Courant quantity ROMS forms as Cg_max in metrics.F. It is what keeps the estimate finite for a run started from rest, where every velocity is zero and the advective limit alone is undefined.

pm and pn are the per-cell 1/dx and 1/dy metric terms rather than the geometry's uniform cell size, so stretched and curvilinear grids give the right answer.

Parameters
[in]levellevel of refinement

void REMORA::extrapolate_metric_to_physical_boundaries ( amrex::MultiFab &  mf,
const amrex::Geometry &  geom,

)

Extrapolate grid metrics to edge of MultiFab, copying the outermost in-domain ghost row outward or, with linear, extending it linearly (steps taken modulo wrap when wrap > 0, for a longitude)

Fill the ghost rows beyond the outermost in-domain ghost row of a cell-centred field at the physical boundaries: by copying that row outward (the default, right for grid metrics and bathymetry), or with linear by extending it from the row inside it (for coordinates, which keep growing past the edge). Used in every build, so it lives here rather than in the NetCDF-only initialisation.

The x passes run first; the y passes then cover every column, including the x strips just filled, which takes care of the corners. The linear mode leaves a periodic direction alone, where FillBoundary has already put the wrapped values in the ghost cells, and its x passes read two columns, so unless y is periodic they are limited to the rows those columns hold data in (the domain and its ring). The copy mode is what it always was: it reads only the ring and covers the full extent in every direction.

Parameters
[in,out]mfmultifab of data to extrapolate on
[in]geomgeometry
[in]linearextend linearly instead of copying
[in]wrapperiod to take the linear step modulo (360 for a longitude), 0 for none

The boundary-condition half of FillPatch: physical and NetCDF boundary conditions, periodic corners and the free-slip top, for a MultiFab whose fine-fine ghost cells are already filled. Lets several fields share one exchange.

The boundary-condition half of FillPatch, for a MultiFab whose fine-fine (and, above level 0, coarse-fine) ghost cells are already filled: physical boundary conditions, boundary data from NetCDF files, periodic corners, and free-slip at the top for the face-centered velocities. Split out so that several fields can share one exchange and then take their conditions in turn (advance_2d does this for ubar, vbar and zeta).

◆ init_biology_ic()

void REMORA::init_biology_ic ( int  lev)

Initialize biology tracers from whichever source remora.biology_ic_type selects. Call after the physical fields exist: the analytic profiles are functions of temperature.

Initialize the biology tracers from whichever source remora.biology_ic_type selects.

Deliberately decoupled from remora.ic_type. A NetCDF initial file supplies only the tracers it happens to contain – the BioToy file has oxygen but no PO4 or ODU – so validating an option set the file does not cover would otherwise mean regenerating binary input that no fresh clone can reproduce. With biology_ic_type = analytic the physical fields still come from NetCDF while biology comes from the problem's analytic profile.

Must be called after the physical fields are initialized: the analytic biology profiles are functions of temperature.

Parameters
[in]levlevel to initialize on

void REMORA::init_full_domain_from_analytic ( )

Initialize high-resolution initial data, zeta included, from analytic functions.

Evaluate the analytic initial state, free surface, and biology on the full domain at hires_init_level and average them down to level 0.

That level does not exist yet, so its coordinates are built here: x_r and y_r from the cell size (constant grid scale), z_r and z_w from the free surface and the bathymetry. The bathymetry is the hires grid data when hires_grid_level >= hires_init_level, and the analytic bathymetry evaluated at hires_init_level otherwise.

void REMORA::inject_mask_outside_domain ( int  lev)

Give lev's rho-mask ghost cells beyond the domain the coarser level's values.

Overwrite lev's rho-mask ghost cells beyond the domain edge with the coarser level's mask there, injected piecewise-constant.

FillCoarsePatchPC fills those cells with foextrap, which copies the interior outward, even across a periodic edge. At a river mouth on a wall that turns the land behind the river wet, and the clamped boundary's salt then mixes into the river cell; at a periodic edge it ignores whatever lies across the seam. Level 0 takes these cells from its grid file, or from a periodic FillBoundary, so the coarser level's ghost cells hold the right mask.

◆ interp_grid_coords_from_coarse()

void REMORA::interp_grid_coords_from_coarse ( int  lev,
amrex::MultiFab &  fine,
const amrex::MultiFab &  crse 
)

Fill a refined level's coordinate array (lon, lat, angle) from the coarser level, including the ghost cells outside the domain.

Fill a refined level's coordinate array from the coarser level, ghost cells included.

FillCoarsePatch would finish with the physical boundary condition pm and pn want, which copies the edge value into every ghost cell outside the domain and averages the corners; for a coordinate that puts those cells on top of the edge rather than where they are. Here the ghost cells outside the domain are interpolated like the rest, from the coarse level's own ghost cells, which hold the coordinates continued past the edge (extrapolate_metric_to_physical_boundaries with linear on level 0, and this function on the levels between). The coarse level has NGROW+1 ghost cells, enough for the stencil at any refinement ratio from 2 up. The interpolation is conservative-linear, which reproduces a linear field exactly.

The coarse data is copied without periodicity. Across a periodic edge, FillBoundary has already put the wrapped values in the coarse ghost cells, but a ghost cell that also lies beyond a wall (a corner where the seam meets a non-periodic face) keeps the value continued from the file's ring, while its periodic image keeps the other side's. A periodic copy would give that cell both as sources, and which one wins is not defined: on a GPU it varies from run to run (#775). Copied without periodicity, each cell comes from the coarse level's own ghost cell. The fine level's ghost cells across a periodic edge are then refilled from its valid cells, wrapped as on level 0.

[in,out]fineits coordinate array
[in]crsethe coarser level's

◆ level0_refine_footprint()

BoxList REMORA::level0_refine_footprint ( bool &  unbounded) const

Level-0 index region a finer level may need; unbounded if it can go anywhere.

The level-0 cells whose boxes a finer level needs kept: every refinement indicator's region, in level-0 index space, as AMReX's grid generation sees it. AMReX buffers the tagged cells by amr.n_error_buf, rounds them to blocks of amr.blocking_factor (of level 1) over the refinement ratio, and clears every tag within amr.n_proper such blocks of a cell no level-0 box covers. So a dropped box that close to an indicator would clip the fine grids the full-domain run makes. The region is therefore the indicator's cells plus the buffer, rounded out to whole blocks, grown by n_proper + 1 blocks, and then by the coarse stencil of the coarse-fine fills and the flux register. A box touching it is never dropped, so the fine grids, and the coarse data under and around them, are those of the full-domain run. Level 1 only: drop_dry_level0_boxes drops nothing when amr.max_level > 1, since a level-2 indicator grows level 1 by its own buffer and proper nesting, which this does not follow.

Parameters
[out]unboundedtrue when an indicator has no region, so a finer level may go anywhere

set this level's barotropic contact points from its parent, mass-conservingly

Set the normal barotropic velocity on this level's coarse-fine interface from the parent's time-averaged mass flux, as ROMS does in put_refine2d (nesting.F): 

ubar_f = Dubar_c / D_f,    D_f = 0.5*(h + zeta)_{i-1} + 0.5*(h + zeta)_i

D comes from know; ROMS instead uses one time index for both sides: u2dbc_im.F's nested branch builds D from zeta(kout) and writes ubar(kout), and put_refine2d uses indx1 for both. )

Keep advance_3d's W, as omega, for the particles to advect with, if any species advects on this level.

Particles are advected in terrain-following coordinates, so they need omega, the velocity across the w-levels, rather than a Cartesian vertical velocity. As in ROMS floats, it comes from the time-averaged fluxes update_massflux_3d leaves, the ones the tracers move with, rather than the diagnostic omega from the current velocities. advance_3d integrates those fluxes into W, the same volume flux compute_omega would build, its first ghost column included, so this keeps W scaled by pm*pn instead of integrating the columns again. The scaling and fill are those of compute_omega, so the result is the same to the bit.

◆ zero_level0_dry_ghost_cells()

void REMORA::zero_level0_dry_ghost_cells ( )

Zero those cells in every level-0 field (see set_dry_ghost_cells)

With level-0 boxes dropped, the ghost cells of a kept box that lie in a dropped box are never filled by an exchange, and the land stencils of the kept box read them. What those stencils compute stays on land only while the values there are finite: a wet cell is at least NGROW+2 land cells away and the masks multiply the land values out (the regression tests write 7 there and compare), but 0 * NaN is NaN, so a NaN there spreads into the water within a few steps. A fresh FArrayBox holds NaN in a debug build (amrex.init_snan), so these cells are zeroed in every level-0 field as soon as the fields exist, before anything reads them. Fields made later on the level-0 layout (lon/lat/angle from the grid file, the rho-point surface stress) zero theirs when they are allocated.

The scratch MultiFabs the step allocates on the level-0 layout (for example in setup_step, gls, bulk_fluxes and the prestep) are not zeroed there. Nothing that the step reads from them in a dropped region reaches a kept cell's result: the Debug CI build (amrex.init_snan) and the dropped-vs-full feature checks with signalling NaNs and the invalid, zero and overflow traps on all complete with bitwise water points. A new kernel that reads such scratch in its ghost cells and lets the value reach a wet cell would break that; zero the scratch with set_dry_ghost_cells then.

average the fine velocity onto the coarse over ROMS's nine-point stencil (fine2coarse2d, half-width (Rscale-1)/2 in both directions) instead of only the faces that tile the coarse face. average the fine tracers onto the coarse weighted by cell volume, Hz/(pm*pn), rather than by area as ROMS's fine2coarse3d does. Off by default. Where the fine layer thickness varies under a coarse cell, as interpolated bathymetry near land makes it, the area mean gains or loses tracer content. Volume weighting keeps it only where the coarse cell's volume matches the fine volumes under it, so not at a coast, and it is not applied to the initial high-resolution cascade (average_down_with_grow_cells).

0 = never impose the 2D coarse-fine interface condition, 1 = every fast step, 2 = only the first fast step of each baroclinic step.

1 matches ROMS and is the default: put_refine2d runs once before the barotropic loop, but u2dbc_im re-applies the same mass-flux formula on every fast step inside it, so 2 is only half the ROMS schedule. On the dogbone, 2 helps early and is much worse later.

The solver, the FillPatch time interpolation, and the kernels only ever see elapsed time, which stays small enough for a float to resolve a timestep. Anything that needs a time on the model clock – forcing and boundary files, the calendar, output time stamps, user-given times – goes through model_time() in double.
